title: Fluctuations of topological charges in two-dimensional classical Heisenberg model through high-temperature and low-temperature expansions
abstract: It is well known that KT transition in 2d XY model is driven by the binding and unbinding of topological defects, which can be characterized by the fluctuation of topological charges inside a region. We extend the idea into the 2d Heisenberg model and calculate the fluctuation through high-temperature and low-temperature expansion respectively. It is found that the fluctuation of topological charges is proportional to the area of the region at high temperatures while obeys the perimeter law at low temperatures.
summary: This paper analyzes the fluctuation of topological charges in the 2D classical Heisenberg model using both high-temperature and low-temperature expansions. The key finding is that these fluctuations follow an area law at high temperatures but switch to a perimeter law at low temperatures, suggesting a phase transition analogous to the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition.
main_problem: The study investigates how topological charge fluctuations behave in the two-dimensional classical Heisenberg model, aiming to draw parallels with the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition observed in the 2D XY model.
main_result: The fluctuation of topological charges exhibits an area law ($\propto L^2$) at high temperatures and transitions to a perimeter law ($\propto L$) at low temperatures.
method: The analysis employs both high-temperature expansions (diagrammatic techniques) and low-temperature approximations, treating the system in the continuous limit as decoupled free scalar fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is the two-dimensional classical Heisenberg model defined by the Hamiltonian $H = -J \sum_{\langle ij angle} \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \mathbf{S}_j$. At low temperatures, it is approximated in the continuous limit as a Gaussian field theory.
key_observables: Topological charge fluctuation ($\chi$), defined as $\langle Q^2 angle - \langle Q angle^2$, and the topological charge $Q$ itself.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$) or inverse temperature ($ eta = 1/k_B T$), and the linear dimension of the region ($L$).
main_assumptions: The high-temperature expansion is carried out up to $O( eta^4)$, and the low-temperature regime assumes spins fluctuate around the z-axis, leading to a continuum approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 defines the lattice structure and topological charge $ho_{ij}$. Figure 2 illustrates diagrams contributing to correlation functions used in the calculation.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem by relating it to the KT transition. It then details calculations using high-temperature expansions, followed by a separate treatment using low-temperature approximations that map the system onto free scalar fields. The results are compared to show the scaling laws for $\chi$.
why_interesting: The study of topological excitations and their fluctuations is central to understanding phase transitions in many quantum systems, making this relevant to theories involving emergent order parameters or critical phenomena.
